argument: Parses as (_LOCK_FLAGS ^ O_CREAT) | O_EXCL, and X ^ Y == X | Y whenever X & Y == 0. _LOCK_FLAGS = O_RDWR|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC (decisions.py:67; O_CLOEXEC falls back to 0, still disjoint) shares no bit with O_CREAT: Darwin 0x2|0x100|0x1000000 vs 0x200; Linux 0x2|0x20000(x86-64)/0x8000(arm64)|0x80000 vs 0x40. So os.open gets the identical int on every supported platform (Windows is not one: the module needs os.O_NOFOLLOW and dir_fd), and nothing about the syscall, its result or its errors can differ. (Constants are from the system fcntl.h headers; no test asserts them at runtime.) No input to _lock_file (name, dir_fd, existing/absent/symlinked lock file) changes the flag value, which is fixed at import, so no behavior test can tell the two apart.
